column2: DANGER Wing Fuel Tank Access Panel Sign – Fuel Vapor Escapes When Panel Opens – 8x12 Aluminum
column3:
Fuel Vapor Escapes When Panel Opens. This DANGER Wing Fuel Tank Access Panel sign from CGAP Safety reads: WING TANK ACCESS PANEL / FUEL VAPOR ESCAPES / WHEN PANEL IS REMOVED / NO IGNITION SOURCES NEARBY. Written for aircraft MRO hangars, FBOs, airline maintenance bases and military maintenance contractors.

Why this sign matters

Removing access panels on a defueled tank releases trapped jet fuel vapor that a spark, light or hot tool can ignite at the opening.

Where to post it

Lower wing at tank access panel rows and tank entry staging area.

Who orders it

Aircraft MRO maintenance manager, hangar safety lead.

Rust-resistant .065 aluminum, UV-resistant print, pre-drilled in all four corners. Made in the USA. Related standards to review for your site: NFPA 410 fuel tank entry; OEM AMM tank entry procedure; 29 CFR 1910.146. A sign supports your safety program; it does not replace guarding, lockout or training.

column2: DANGER Center Tank Inerting System Sign – Nitrogen-Enriched Air Displaces Oxygen – 8x12 Aluminum

This DANGER Center Tank Inerting System sign from CGAP Safety reads: FUEL TANK INERTING SYSTEM / NITROGEN ENRICHED AIR / NOT ENOUGH OXYGEN TO LIVE / DEACTIVATE SYSTEM THEN / VENTILATE AND TEST TO ENTER. Why this sign matters

The inerting system fills the tank ullage with nitrogen-enriched air, so an entrant can lose consciousness from low oxygen if the system is not deactivated and the tank ventilated.

Where to post it

At the inerting system bay and center tank access.

Who orders it

Aircraft MRO maintenance manager, hangar safety lead, airline heavy maintenance.

Rust-resistant .065 aluminum, UV-resistant print, pre-drilled in all four corners. Made in the USA. Related standards to review for your site: 14 CFR 25.981 flammability reduction; OEM AMM system deactivation; 29 CFR 1910.146.
